new_sources.title: Curie: Toward Rigorous and Automated Scientific Experimentation with AI Agents
EXP-Bench: Can AI Conduct AI Research Experiments?
AdaEvolve: Adaptive LLM Driven Zeroth-Order Optimization
Harnessing agent memory to build lifelong AI partners for materials scientists
Test-Time Self-Evolution in Multi-Agent Systems for Materials Discovery
Inference-Time Scaling of Verification: Self-Evolving Deep Research Agents via Test-Time Rubric-Guided Verification
Autonomous Research Agents: A Survey of AI Scientists and the Verification Gap

candidate_mechanisms.description: Treat search policy, not only candidate solutions, as an adaptive object. AdaEvolve uses one accumulated-improvement signal to modulate local explore/exploit intensity, allocate budget across islands, spawn islands, and trigger high-level tactic generation on stagnation. EvoX goes further by representing the search strategy itself as an evolvable object and changing parent selection, inspiration construction, and variation operators based on measured progress and population state, without resetting accumulated solutions.
quantitative_evidence: AdaEvolve on Frontier-CS (172 tasks, GPT-5, equal 50-call budget): mean 61.33 and median 75.15 versus OpenEvolve 50.75/56.37, ShinkaEvolve 47.79/46.22, GEPA 43.04/33.68, and single-call GPT-5 20.64/0.

AdaEvolve ablations, three runs each: Circle Packing full 2.6294±0.003; without local adaptation 2.5906±0.048; without adaptive island selection 2.6180±0.005; without meta-guidance 2.5213±0.028. Signal Processing full 0.7178±0.019; without local adaptation 0.6807±0.021; without adaptive island selection 0.619±0.0541; without meta-guidance 0.5476±0.011. Fixed 2 or 5 islands also underperform full system on both tasks.

EvoX reports strongest overall performance on 196 tasks; on Frontier-CS mean 62.6, median 75.5, with reported 24%/34% mean/median improvement over OpenEvolve. On its signal-processing case study the evolving strategy finishes 34.1% above a static random/free-form baseline under the same 100-iteration budget.

EvoX Heilbronn-triangle ablation: multiple fixed initial strategies saturate while their EvoX-evolved counterparts continue improving. To exceed score 0.031, EvoX and GEPA each require under $1 generation cost versus ShinkaEvolve $7.6 and OpenEvolve $15.4; GEPA plateaus near 0.0323 while EvoX reaches 0.0339.
candidate_mechanisms.evidence_scope: AdaEvolve's clean component ablations are only on Circle Packing and Signal Processing, not all 185 tasks. EvoX's ablation primarily compares fixed versus evolving strategies and initialization/cost behavior on selected tasks; it does not independently isolate every strategy-database or stagnation-trigger component.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: Very high as an external candidate for O's work-loop policy: adapt exploration, branch allocation, and even the search strategy itself from downstream progress/stagnation signals rather than retaining a fixed routing/search heuristic. This is not evidence to adopt raw evolutionary search wholesale; the transferable hypothesis is state-conditional search-policy adaptation with retained evidence/population state.

candidate_mechanisms.description: Distill execution-validated successes into reusable executable skills and recurring failures into inspectable facts/guardrails; retrieve them before expensive actions. Sandbox/job feedback decides what becomes trusted memory, rather than saving model reflection indiscriminately. The memory is portable across sessions and models.
quantitative_evidence: Lifelong-materials-memory: on 49 MatTools questions / 138 executable subtasks, GPT-5.2 task success rose from 44.2% bare to 75.4% after three memory rounds with no parameter update; GPT-5.4 rose 66.7%→88.4%.

Full-system ablation for GPT-5.2 rises 62.3%→75.4% across three rounds, while sandbox-only and memory-only variants remain roughly 57%–60%, supporting interaction between verified execution feedback and durable memory.

A recurring ABACUS wavefunction-initialization failure was converted into a pre-execution guardrail; Sol27LC outcomes improved 22/1/4→25/2/0 Correct/Partial/Error and avoided 91.7% of repeated failures.
Across 13 VASP/LAMMPS workflows, aggregate trace burden fell 17.90M→8.96M tokens and tool calls 1,038→481 by the third round while preserving physically meaningful outputs.
Earlier conference version reports MatTools task accuracy 51.02%→65.31%, subtask accuracy 62.32%→75.36%, runnable rate 97.96%→100%, Round-2 token use -30.8%, and cumulative runtime -22.9%.
candidate_mechanisms.evidence_scope: Materials-science tool use/simulation tasks, with repeated rounds and related-family reuse. Improvements do not prove arbitrary cross-domain research memory transfer. Some evaluations repeat the same task set across rounds, so transfer to genuinely novel tasks should be separately measured.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: Very high for O's durable learning layer: failures should become scoped preconditions/guardrails only after external execution validation; successes can become reusable skills. Also supports keeping learned operational knowledge independent of one model/runtime so O remains replaceable.

candidate_mechanisms.description: Build an explicit failure taxonomy, convert it into detailed verification rubrics, and use a dedicated outcome verifier to produce structured feedback for iterative answer refinement at inference time rather than relying on a vanilla self-judge.
quantitative_evidence: DeepVerifier reportedly improves meta-evaluation F1 by 12%–48% over vanilla agent-as-judge and LLM-judge baselines.
Plug-in test-time verification/refinement yields 8%–11% accuracy gains on challenging GAIA and XBench-DeepResearch subsets with capable closed-source models.
Authors release DeepVerifier-4K with 4,646 curated verification-focused agent steps.
candidate_mechanisms.evidence_scope: Deep-research answer generation rather than full autonomous scientific experimentation; verifier remains model/rubric based and is not an externally validated in-loop scientific oracle.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: High for evaluator design: separate verifier role plus explicit failure categories can outperform generic self-judging, but it must still be calibrated against external ground truth and should not be treated as proof of scientific correctness.

candidate_mechanisms.description: Curie combines intra-agent validation of plan/setup/variables/I-O/reproducibility, inter-agent partitioning and permissible state transitions so unvalidated experiments cannot execute, and a structured experiment knowledge module with DAG/time-machine history rather than relying on conversational recall.
quantitative_evidence: 46 experimental questions across four CS domains, five trials each: Curie weighted averages Design 97.9, Execution Setup 78.1, Implementation Alignment 73.4, Conclusion Correctness 36.1 versus strongest baseline conclusion correctness 10.5, reported as 3.4× improvement.
Paper reports especially large conclusion-accuracy advantages on cloud-compute and ML-training subsets.
candidate_mechanisms.evidence_scope: System-level benchmark; no clean component-level ablation isolating each rigor or knowledge module was found in this scan.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: Medium-high: reinforces that work-state transitions should be evidence-gated and that experiment validity/reproducibility checks belong before downstream conclusions. Later 2026 systems provide stronger component-level evidence for some related mechanisms.

new_failure_evidence.observation: Across 461 tasks from 51 top-tier AI papers, leading agents sometimes score 20%–35% on individual design or implementation aspects, yet complete executable experiment success is only 0.5%.
new_failure_evidence.scope: EXP-Bench's tested 2025 agents and incomplete-starter-code research experiments.
new_failure_evidence.implication: Do not infer autonomous research competence from isolated stage scores. O evaluations should include multiplicative/end-to-end completion and artifact validity, not only local component metrics.

new_failure_evidence.observation: Systematic survey screened 125 works and coded 24 runnable systems: 83% released code, but only 38% released seeds/execution traces and 38% reported novelty verification. Among nine closed-loop L4 systems, seven were mechanical reruns, one was author-claimed without external check, and the survey found no LLM-era system satisfying its rule for an externally validated in-loop oracle.
new_failure_evidence.scope: Survey corpus and its coding rule; this is a field-level audit, not a primary causal experiment.
new_failure_evidence.implication: Treat self-verification gains as internal reliability evidence, not external scientific truth. A genuinely calibrated external or mechanistic oracle remains an open research gap.

new_failure_evidence.observation: Multiple independent evaluations show execution/runnability materially exceeds correct conclusions or complete experimental success. In the materials-memory study GPT-5.4 reaches 89.8% function runnable rate but only 66.7% bare task success and 53.1% question pass; Curie likewise reports substantially higher execution setup than conclusion correctness; EXP-Bench end-to-end success collapses to 0.5% despite partial-stage competence.
new_failure_evidence.scope: The cited benchmarks only; cross-study metric definitions differ and should not be numerically pooled.
new_failure_evidence.implication: O should maintain separate evidence dimensions for syntactic execution, experimental validity, result interpretation, claim provenance, and end-to-end research success.

dead_ends_or_cautions: Do not conflate AdaEvolve and EvoX. AdaEvolve adapts predefined control levels from an improvement signal; EvoX evolves the search strategy representation itself. Their overlap is the broader hypothesis that search control should be state-conditional and adaptive.

Do not interpret EvoX's improvement over fixed strategies as evidence that arbitrary self-modification is beneficial; its strategy candidates are validated and operate under a fixed external evaluator and evaluation budget.

Do not generalize the materials-memory repeated-task gains to arbitrary AGI research. Preserve the distinction between repeated-family guardrail learning, same-benchmark multi-round gains, cross-model transfer, and unseen-domain transfer.
DeepVerifier is a better model-based verifier in its tested setting, not an externally grounded scientific oracle.
The verification-gap survey is useful negative field evidence but should not replace primary-source audits when deciding whether a concrete mechanism works.
next_queries: Find primary systems with externally validated in-loop scientific oracles or mechanistic checkers, not only LLM judges; quantify whether oracle feedback changes downstream research quality.
Search for cross-domain/unseen-task evaluations of validated failure memory and executable skill transfer, especially cases with held-out task families rather than repeated benchmark rounds.
Inspect EvoX strategy-evolution validity checks and failure cases for evaluator exploitation/reward hacking; determine whether adaptive strategy changes can overfit a faulty evaluator.
Search 2026 research-agent systems that jointly adapt search policy and evaluator/verification while keeping those roles causally separable.
Search for rigorous end-to-end experiment benchmarks newer than EXP-Bench and whether 2026 systems materially exceed the 0.5% complete-experiment baseline under matched conditions.
